data.long_meaning: Yaswanth is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, which means 'Lord of the World'. historical_references.reference: Yaswanth was the name of a powerful Chalukya king who ruled the ancient Indian kingdom of Vatapi (present day Badami) from 529 to 545 AD. He is known for his patronage of Jainism and the construction of numerous temples, including the famous cave temples of Badami.
historical_references.context: Ancient Indian kingdom of Vatapi, Badami, Chalukya dynasty, patronage of Jainism, construction of cave temples.

historical_references.reference: Yaswanth is also the name of a 16th century Hindu king of the Vijayanagara Empire, who ruled from 1532 to 1552 AD. He is remembered for his military campaigns against the Deccan Sultanate and his patronage of literature and arts.
